purpose: Preserve sources, distinguish verified/stable facts from volatile claims, and prevent AI assistants from treating fast-moving research snapshots as timeless truth.

verification_status_values.verified: Direct source checked in this run or previously verified primary/official source exists.
verification_status_values.source_present_unchecked: A URL/source name exists but was not manually opened in this run.
verification_status_values.needs_source: Claim lacks a concrete source URL/path and should be sourced before public release.
verification_status_values.conflict_found: Sources disagree or a claim appears outdated/incorrect.
verification_status_values.volatile_reverify: Claim may be correct now but should be rechecked before release or use.

freshness_policy.stable: Math, foundational papers, long-lived definitions; review annually.
freshness_policy.slow_changing: Architecture concepts and mature tools; review each major release cycle.
freshness_policy.fast_moving: APIs, docs, tool behavior, package commands, ComfyUI node names; review before publishing.
freshness_policy.volatile: Model rankings, SOTA claims, hardware releases, benchmark numbers, costs, availability; verify immediately before use.
freshness_policy.historical: Preserve for provenance but do not use as current guidance unless explicitly asked.

ai_usage_rules: Prefer verified sources over synthesized lane summaries when answering factual questions.
Use volatile claims only with date/edition qualifiers unless freshly verified.
If canonical lane text conflicts with a primary or official source, prefer the primary/official source and flag the conflict.
Do not remove sources during editorial cleanup; move stale sources to historical/provenance only.
When a claim lacks a source URL/path, answer cautiously and mark it as an AIWF research note rather than confirmed external fact.
